landlock_probe.interpretation: Runtime enforcement must probe actual host support; this hosted result is not evidence about Andreas' Ubuntu developer host.

experiments.setup: Parent opened a mode-0600 temporary file, then launched a uid/gid-65534 child. Direct path open was denied but the writable file descriptor was deliberately inherited with pass_fds.
experiments.supports: Path-access restrictions alone do not define effective child authority when pre-opened handles exist.

experiments.setup: Same privilege-drop control without passing the protected file descriptor.
experiments.supports: The successful inherited-FD write depended on the authority carrier, not on path access.

experiments.setup: Parent launched a uid/gid-65534 child with a Unix socket and sent the already-open protected file descriptor after launch via SCM_RIGHTS.
experiments.supports: Post-launch IPC can transfer effective authority even when pathname access is unavailable.

experiments.model: Random parent grants, child requests and ambient authority carriers over path, carrier, kernel and resource effect atoms.
experiments.boundary: Zero escapes in this abstract model is not proof of Linux enforcement completeness or end-to-end safety.

negative_results: Landlock could not be exercised in the hosted execution environment because the direct availability probe returned ENOSYS.
No end-to-end enforcement stack was executed on Andreas' Ubuntu developer system in this run.
The carrier-aware abstract model does not model kernel bugs, TOCTOU, all IPC types, all FFI, side channels, broker defects or every Linux object class.
